newsitem.title: UK: RMC, Redland off on German data, strong stg.
newsitem.headline: RMC, Redland off on German data, strong stg.

text.p: Shares in building materials groups Redland Plc and RMC Group Plc were knocked to their lowest levels in a year on Thursday, hit by weak German economic data and worries about sterling's strength, traders said.
Redland fell 7-1/2p to 337 by 1600 GMT while RMC was down 29p at 939.

Dealers said German data which showed a rise in unemployment to 10.8 percent in December and a fall in GDP growth to 1.4 percent in 1996 from 1.9 percent the previous year had dampened sentiment. Both firms have a high exposure to Germany.

"The sector has been weak for the last couple of days and these worries about Germany have been revived today," one market-maker said. "There have been a lot of sellers and we've seen a lot of stock doing the rounds."
One market-maker said there had been talk of a Merrill Lynch downgrade on Redland but Merrill construction analyst Kevin Cammack said he could "categorically deny" downgrading the stock.
"Sterling worries are still on the boil and aren't helping the sector," another market-maker said. "The sector just hasn't been doing too well recently."
On Wednesday, NatWest Securities cut its 1996 profit forecasts for RMC to 266 million stg from 286 million because of sterling's strength.
